# Variance memo: Aramex FY2025 vs FY2024

*Generated by `src/fpa.py` from the published results. Every figure below is computed, not typed.*

## Headline
- Revenue AED 6,359.9m, +0.6% (AED 35.5m).
- Gross profit AED 1,449.5m, -4.1%; gross margin 23.9% -> 22.8%.
- Normalized EBIT AED 237.7m, -19.9%; reported EBIT AED 192.7m after AED 45.0m of one-off costs.
- Reported net profit AED 20.6m (-85%); normalized AED 85.0m.

## Revenue: what moved
- Biggest gain: Domestic Express AED 157.6m (+9.4%). Biggest drop: International Express AED -268.2m (-11.1%).
- International Express: shipments 28.1m -> 23.6m. Volume alone would have cut revenue by AED 386.3m; higher revenue per shipment (AED 85.9 -> 90.9) recovered AED 118.1m.
- Domestic Express: shipments 111.3m -> 119.8m added AED 128.7m; revenue per shipment AED 15.14 -> 15.39.

## Gross margin: mix vs rate
- Across the four products, gross margin moved -1.05 pp. Of that, **mix** (revenue shifting from high-margin International Express to lower-margin products) explains -0.59 pp and **rate** (margins changing within products) -0.46 pp.
- International Express lost AED 104.0m of gross profit: AED 86.8m from lower revenue and AED 17.2m from a lower margin rate.
- Logistics added AED 34.3m: AED 12.6m from growth and AED 21.7m from a better margin (15.5% -> 19.5%).
- Domestic Express grew revenue but its margin fell (23.6% -> 22.0%), costing AED 29.6m.
- Freight Forwarding's margin dip (12.8% -> 12.5%) is mainly an accounting reclassification of transaction fees from overheads into direct costs, according to the company, so not a real deterioration.

## Overheads
- Normalized overheads (gross profit minus normalized EBIT) were AED 1,211.7m vs AED 1,215.5m (-0.3%), so the EBIT decline is a gross-profit problem, not a cost-control problem.

## 2026 scenarios (illustrative drivers, not guidance)
- Downside: revenue AED 6,184.1m, gross margin 21.6%, normalized EBIT AED 121.1m (2.0%).
- Base: revenue AED 6,488.0m, gross margin 22.4%, normalized EBIT AED 240.1m (3.7%).
- Upside: revenue AED 6,684.0m, gross margin 23.1%, normalized EBIT AED 334.1m (5.0%).

## So what
- More than half of the margin decline is mix (56%): the high-margin long-haul business is shrinking while regional products grow. Watch International Express revenue per shipment and Domestic Express margin recovery.
- Logistics is the profit engine to scale: highest growth and the biggest margin improvement.
